description:
Why this choice is correct: the &self receiver on AiaFetcher::fetch (pkix-aia/src/lib.rs:566) is the load-bearing call that admits caller-side caching without any trait-surface acknowledgment. Caching wrappers use RefCell (single-threaded) or Mutex/RwLock (concurrent) for interior mutability, fitting through the &self bound. AGENTS.md non-negotiable #6 explicitly requires this design: 'Callbacks not closed structs. … Do not collapse callbacks into closed structs that hide the seam.'

A future contributor might suggest changing the receiver to &mut self ('clearer when the impl actually mutates internal state'). That change would break every caching wrapper and force callers to put the entire fetcher behind a Mutex. Reject any such proposal: the &self bound IS the caching seam.

The CachingFetcher doctest at lines 503-525 demonstrates the pattern using no_std-portable BTreeMap+RefCell. This doctest should be defended too — it is the executable specification for 'here is how you actually wrap this trait'.
title: Decision: &self receiver on AiaFetcher admits interior-mutability caching wrappers
